items.title: 56711_Buster Smith oral history interview
items.q: Johnny Hodges came in with all that beautiful playing and that big tone and everything, and he had a lot of cats trying to copy behind him.

ctx.x: Do you think, though, to any extent at all that this very competitive attitude among musicians is one of the things that made Jazz advance musically very fast? Do you think that it actually helped the music? It was bad for the musicians, but do you think it was good for the music?

Well, in a way... I'll tell you what. They can say what they want. But mostly when them styles change, it's mostly back West somewhere. Like Kansas City come up with that different kind of jump. And most of the musicians, it comes back out West here. Like, Charlie Parker came in there with that new way of playing. Yeah, all right.
